title: How to Preach Christ From the Old Testament
subtitle: How to preach Christ from the Old Testament with integrity, using redemptive history and typology instead of forced allegory or flat moralizing, in practical sermon terms.

sections.title: Why You Cannot Preach the Old Testament as if Christ Never Came
sections.body:
Jesus said the whole Old Testament was about him. He did not say some of it. He said all of it.

On the Emmaus road, with two heartbroken disciples, he began with Moses and all the Prophets and explained what was said in all the Scriptures concerning himself. That is a staggering claim. The law, the histories, the psalms, the prophets, the strange and the dull and the violent, all of it pointing forward to a cross outside Jerusalem. If that is true, then to preach an Old Testament text and never arrive at Christ is to stop short of what the text was for.

This is the great failure of much Old Testament preaching. We treat the passage as a closed museum of ancient lessons. Be brave like David. Be faithful like Ruth. Be patient like Job. We turn the Scriptures into a gallery of moral heroes and miss the one figure the whole collection was painting. The Old Testament is not a book of examples with God in the background. It is the long account of God preparing to rescue a people he would not give up on. Preach it as if Christ never came and you have preached someone else's Bible.

sections.title: Stop Turning Saints Into Self-Help
sections.body:
The most common error is the most respectable. We moralize.

It sounds biblical. Take Daniel in the lions den and the application writes itself. Dare to be a Daniel. Stand firm when the culture pressures you. There is truth in it, and that is exactly what makes it dangerous, because it stops at the man and never reaches the God who shut the lions mouths. The story is not first about Daniel courage. It is about a God who preserves his servant in the pit, a God who would one day go into a deeper pit himself and not be preserved, so that we could be.

Moralizing makes the hero the point and makes you the project. Be more like him. Try harder. And the people leave measuring themselves against a giant and falling short, with no gospel to lift them. The Bible is full of flawed people, and the flaws are not accidents. David is an adulterer. Abraham is a liar. Jacob is a cheat. If the point were be like them, the book would be a poor manual. The point is that God keeps his covenant through people who cannot keep theirs, and that points in only one direction.

sections.title: Stop Forcing Jesus Into Every Detail
sections.body:
The overcorrection is just as bad. Having learned to find Christ, we start finding him in the curtain rings.

This is the preacher who turns the scarlet cord of Rahab into the blood of Christ, the two spies into the two witnesses, the window into the wounded side. The congregation is impressed, and they should not be, because nothing in the text invited any of it. This is allegory, and allegory will prove anything because it is accountable to nothing. Once you decide the details mean whatever you need them to mean, the text has lost its authority and you have gained it.

The difference between typology and allegory is discipline. Typology follows connections the Scripture itself draws or that redemptive history makes legitimate. The Passover lamb points to Christ because the New Testament says so and because the pattern is built into the event. The scarlet cord points to nothing in particular because nobody but the preacher said it did. Ask whether your line to Christ runs along the grain of the whole story or whether you carved it yourself with a clever knife. If you built it, take it out. Cleverness is not the same as faithfulness.

sections.title: The Honest Roads From the Text to Christ
sections.body:
There are real bridges, not invented ones. Learn the legitimate roads and you will not need the tricks.

The road of promise. The Old Testament is full of promises that strain forward and are answered only in Christ. The seed of the woman, the offspring of Abraham, the throne of David, the new covenant Jeremiah saw from a distance. Trace the promise to its fulfillment and the line is the text own.

The road of type. God built patterns into the history. The exodus, the Passover, the temple, the sacrificial system, the prophet and priest and king. Each one is a shadow cast backward by a reality not yet arrived. Show the shadow, then show the substance, and let the people feel the weight of how long God had been preparing.

The road of contrast. Sometimes the bridge is failure. Every king disappoints. Every priest dies. Every covenant is broken from the human side. The Old Testament keeps raising a hope and then showing you it cannot deliver, and the ache it creates is the ache only Christ resolves. Promise, type, contrast. Walk the roads the text laid down and you will preach Christ without forcing a single verse.

sections.title: How to Actually Build the Sermon
sections.body:
Christ-centered preaching is not a trick you bolt on at the end. It is a way of reading you bring to the start.

First, preach the text in its own moment. Do not rush to Jesus before you have honored what the passage meant to the people who first heard it. Let the exile feel like exile. Let the famine be a real famine. The original meaning is not an obstacle to the gospel. It is the foundation of it, and a leap to Christ that skips the actual text is a leap of avoidance.

Then ask where this sits in the story. Every passage has a location in the one long account that runs from a garden to a city, from a fall to a redemption. Find where you are standing in that account, and the road to Christ usually appears on its own, because the whole thing was always moving toward him.

Then cross with integrity, by promise or type or contrast, never by a clever leap. And land the application in grace, not in effort. The Old Testament saint is not your example to copy first. He is a witness to the God who saves, and that God has a name, and the name is Jesus. Preach the whole Bible as the one story it is, and your people will meet Christ on every page he is actually on.
